recipes.name: Sausage and Egg Casserole
ingredients_raw: 6 slices white bread, cut into 1/2-inch cubes

steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir in sausage. Cook and stir until sausage is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink, about 10 minutes. Drain and discard any excess grease.
Beat eggs in a large bowl; stir in milk, salt, and mustard.
Fold bread cubes, Cheddar cheese, and sausage into the egg mixture.
Pour into a lightly greased 7x11-inch baking dish. Cover and refrigerate, 8 hours to overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Remove casserole from the refrigerator 30 minutes before baking.
Bake in the preheated oven until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sausage and Egg Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This sausage and egg casserole is the perfect combination of eggs, sausage, bread, and cheese. Everyone loves this tender and delicious recipe.

review.reviewBody: Very easy, make ahead and tasty too! This is one of those recipes where you can customize it to suit your taste - add onions or other meats & veggies if you want. I made this for Faceless Frenzy July 2012. Thanks for a good recipe to eat and photograph.

This is our go to for breakfast casserole. So versatile. we've switched up this recipe so many different ways depending on what's on hand. bacon instead of sausage. hashbrowns instead of bread cubes. Mushrooms, green peppers and onions. And our favorite, fresh spinach. I've even made it a little more Mexican with Rotel and a can of chopped green chilis. We've been using this one for years and years! Thanks for such a versatile recipe

Love this recipe but you tweak it to make your own. There are so many variations. I used lb. of Bass Sausage ( my preference because of very little grease.(drain fat) which isn't much with this brand of sausage, brown it and added green onion, bell pepper, sweet onion and leeks sauté diced very thin, use as much and whatever veggies as you prefer. I cut-up potatoes bread (instead of using real potatoes to save time)into cubes and toasted in the oven with butter until golden brown (6-8 slices). Set it a side . I added the wet ingredients which consist of 2 cups of heavy cream and 6 eggs adding 8oz of Cabot Vermont Sharp white/Shred half and add to cream, season with salt and pepper a little garlic powder . Butter your casserole dish and place the toasted bread at the bottom of the pan, ladle the sausage mixture over the bread evenly then pour the heavy cream/cheese mixture over that and shred the remaining cheese and add on top then place in the oven at 400 degrees for an hour or until golden brown and bubbly. Let set for 10 min before cutting allowing your casserole to set.

I’ve been having variations of this dish for over 20 years. I made a few changes to fit the appetite of my family. I use cubed potato’s versus bread. You can use shredded hash browns as well. It’s more filling. I don’t find myself eating 4 pieces. Just 2. I also add 1/2 of a large onion. 1 green, 1 red and 1 yellow pepper. To add a little zest I use spicy sausage. If it was just for myself, I would add some type of spicy pepper as well. My entire family loves this. It doesn’t last a day. Some eat it through the entire day. It refrigerates well. When I make double batches I freeze the the second batch in portions of 2.

I've been making this for about 30 years - found the recipe in a small (Betty Crocker maybe?) supermarket aisle Christmas recipe book. Anyway - my family loves it and this has become a Christmas breakfast tradition. At Thanksgiving I pick up an extra bag of stuffing cubes (unseasoned) and toss it in the freezer. I use the cubes for this recipe (saves time cutting bread into cubes). I open the bag a few hours before assembling to dry it out a bit. You can add any veggie or meat you like and switch up the cheese if desired. Allows for a wide range of creativity. Really good, quick and easy to assemble and tastes really good the next day as leftovers (if there are any)! Try this, you'll like it and thank yourself on Christmas morning when you aren't standing in front of a stove!
I have made this over 30 years. Boil the sausage. Use 8 slices of bread cubed with no crust. Use 2 cups cheddar. The way posted is too soupy. Cut the milk down to 2 cups too.

This was absolutely delicious! I didn't have time to let it sit for hours so I took the advice of another reviewer and let the bread soak while I cooked the sausage. I added onion and some bell pepper to give it a little more flavor and color and baked it about 45 minutes. Hubby loved it and there's lots left over for breakfast and dinner tomorrow.

Interesting recipe but but the basic recipe would be a little lacking in flavor. I suppose if you used a very spicy sausage it might help. I added onion, green peppers and black pepper to bring it up a notch.

Excellent after adding peppers, onions, and black pepper to the mix. Used sourdough bread for the white bread. Added extra cheese to the top before popping it in the oven. We and our guests had this casserole for brunch today and everyone thought it was delicious. Bake time sat least 50 minutes though. Allowing it a few minutes (5 or so) to rest after baking is essential.

Wonderful basic recipe, I increased it to serve 12, added green onion, green and red peppers chopped, and some chopped tomato for color and extra taste---got all rave remarks. Would be good with any meat or veggie additions. It baked in the time alloted, and I added 15 minutes "rest time" before slicing into servings. LOOKED as good as it tasted, another star:)

Not a bad egg and sausage casserole however I wish I had put some veggies like onion, garlic, and maybe spinach to give it more variety. I would also recommend using breakfast sausage with herb seasoning for better flavor. 
Also, if using a deep glass baking dish adjust cooking time accordingly. I added 30 more minutes. I might use a 7x11 next time.

When I was in grad school and pinching Pennie’s I ate this a lot. So this recipe contains an element of nostalgia. I make it exactly according to the recipe, so I tend to save some older bread to make my own breadcrumbs. You’re not gonna go wrong with this one so enjoy.
Perfect
Old school dish and easy to make
The only change I made was adding onions and bell pepper. Absolutely fantastic. A great breakfast and a wonderful supper that can be thrown together and left in the fridge all day.
Wonderful and simple to make.
I followed the recipe as directed. I added green onions and celery for variety, I tried to upload pictures but the program rejected my file

This is a great recipe! It is so nice to prep the night before and just pop it in the oven that morning. It's very similar to one from Southern Living magazine that I used some years ago. That recipe also called for 1/4 tsp Worcestershire sauce which I find adds to the deliciousness. I also use diced ham instead of sausage, which I find less greasy and easier.
This is our Christmas morning tradition. My mom made this every christmas. She passed away this year and my daughter and I made it together this year. You can taste the love in this casserole.
I've been making this for about 10 years now for special occasions. It's awesome!
